Laboratorio 9: Redes Neuronales Artificiales — SmartStay Advisors

Jonathan Díaz, Martín Pérez, Karen Toledo

2026-05-10

Enlace del repositorio: https://github.com/Jonialen/cosas-mineria

Referencia de la base de datos: Moro, S., Rita, P., & Cortez, P. (2014). Bank Marketing [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5K306.

library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
library(janitor)
library(GGally)
library(corrplot)
library(gridExtra)
library(scales)
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(recipes)
library(fastDummies)
library(psych)
library(reshape2)

1 Diseño experimental y preparación de los datos

1.1 Carga del conjunto de datos

bank <- read.csv("bank.csv", sep = ";")

# Ver primeras filas
head(bank)
##   age         job marital education default balance housing loan  contact day
## 1  30  unemployed married   primary      no    1787      no   no cellular  19
## 2  33    services married secondary      no    4789     yes  yes cellular  11
## 3  35  management  single  tertiary      no    1350     yes   no cellular  16
## 4  30  management married  tertiary      no    1476     yes  yes  unknown   3
## 5  59 blue-collar married secondary      no       0     yes   no  unknown   5
## 6  35  management  single  tertiary      no     747      no   no cellular  23
##   month duration campaign pdays previous poutcome  y
## 1   oct       79        1    -1        0  unknown no
## 2   may      220        1   339        4  failure no
## 3   apr      185        1   330        1  failure no
## 4   jun      199        4    -1        0  unknown no
## 5   may      226        1    -1        0  unknown no
## 6   feb      141        2   176        3  failure no

1.3 Verificar valores faltantes

# Cantidad de NA por variable
colSums(is.na(bank))
##       age       job   marital education   default   balance   housing      loan 
##         0         0         0         0         0         0         0         0 
##   contact       day     month  duration  campaign     pdays  previous  poutcome 
##         0         0         0         0         0         0         0         0 
##         y 
##         0
# Porcentaje de NA
colSums(is.na(bank))/nrow(bank) * 100
##       age       job   marital education   default   balance   housing      loan 
##         0         0         0         0         0         0         0         0 
##   contact       day     month  duration  campaign     pdays  previous  poutcome 
##         0         0         0         0         0         0         0         0 
##         y 
##         0

1.4 Revisar categorías “unknown”

bank %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.character),
                   ~sum(. == "unknown")))
##   job marital education default housing loan contact month poutcome y
## 1  38       0       187       0       0    0    1324     0     3705 0
bank %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.character),
                   ~mean(. == "unknown") * 100))
##        job marital education default housing loan  contact month poutcome y
## 1 0.840522       0  4.136253       0       0    0 29.28556     0  81.9509 0

1.7 Visualización balance de clases

ggplot(bank, aes(x = y, fill = y)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribución de la variable objetivo",
    x = "Suscripción",
    y = "Frecuencia"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  theme_minimal()

1.9 Histogramas variables numéricas

p1 <- ggplot(bank, aes(age)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(bank, aes(balance)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "darkgreen") +
  theme_minimal()

p3 <- ggplot(bank, aes(duration)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "darkorange") +
  theme_minimal()

p4 <- ggplot(bank, aes(campaign)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "purple") +
  theme_minimal()

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2)

1.10 Boxplots para detectar outliers

p1 <- ggplot(bank, aes(y = age)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(bank, aes(y = balance)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkgreen") +
  theme_minimal()

p3 <- ggplot(bank, aes(y = duration)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkorange") +
  theme_minimal()

p4 <- ggplot(bank, aes(y = campaign)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "purple") +
  theme_minimal()

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2)

1.11 Correlación variables numéricas

cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_vars)

round(cor_matrix, 2)
##            age balance   day duration campaign pdays previous
## age       1.00    0.08 -0.02     0.00    -0.01 -0.01     0.00
## balance   0.08    1.00 -0.01    -0.02    -0.01  0.01     0.03
## day      -0.02   -0.01  1.00    -0.02     0.16 -0.09    -0.06
## duration  0.00   -0.02 -0.02     1.00    -0.07  0.01     0.02
## campaign -0.01   -0.01  0.16    -0.07     1.00 -0.09    -0.07
## pdays    -0.01    0.01 -0.09     0.01    -0.09  1.00     0.58
## previous  0.00    0.03 -0.06     0.02    -0.07  0.58     1.00

1.12 Heatmap correlaciones

corrplot(
  cor_matrix,
  method = "color",
  type = "upper",
  tl.col = "black",
  tl.srt = 45
)

1.19 Matriz de pares (sample)

set.seed(123)

bank_sample <- bank %>%
  sample_n(1000)

GGally::ggpairs(
  bank_sample,
  columns = c("age", "balance", "duration", "campaign"),
  aes(color = y, alpha = 0.5)
)

2.13 Eliminar variable duration

La duración puede causar data leakage porque la duración de la llamada está altamente relacionada con la respuesta.

bank_processed_no_duration <- bank_processed %>%
  select(-duration)

dim(bank_processed_no_duration)
## [1] 4521   42

        mediana = median,
        desviacion = sd,
        minimo = min,
        maximo = max

      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

3.4 Gráfico balance de clases

ggplot(bank, aes(x = y, fill = y)) +
  geom_bar() +
  geom_text(
    stat = "count",
    aes(label = after_stat(count)),
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribución de la variable objetivo",
    x = "Suscripción",
    y = "Cantidad"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  theme_minimal()

3.5 Histogramas variables numéricas

num_vars <- bank %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

num_vars_long <- melt(num_vars)

ggplot(num_vars_long, aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribución de variables numéricas",
    x = "Valor",
    y = "Frecuencia"
  )

3.6 Detección visual de outliers

ggplot(num_vars_long, aes(y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkorange") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Detección de outliers",
    y = "Valores"
  )

3.21 Prueba Chi-cuadrado

chisq.test(bank$job, bank$y)
## 
##  Pearson's Chi-squared test
## 
## data:  bank$job and bank$y
## X-squared = 68.988, df = 11, p-value = 1.901e-10
chisq.test(bank$education, bank$y)
## 
##  Pearson's Chi-squared test
## 
## data:  bank$education and bank$y
## X-squared = 15.237, df = 3, p-value = 0.001625
chisq.test(bank$housing, bank$y)
## 
##  Pearson's Chi-squared test with Yates' continuity correction
## 
## data:  bank$housing and bank$y
## X-squared = 48.885, df = 1, p-value = 2.715e-12

3.22 Comparación estadística numérica

t.test(age ~ y, data = bank)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  age by y
## t = -2.5024, df = 604.47, p-value = 0.0126
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group no and group yes is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -2.6653503 -0.3213752
## sample estimates:
##  mean in group no mean in group yes 
##          40.99800          42.49136
t.test(balance ~ y, data = bank)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  balance by y
## t = -1.4347, df = 752.36, p-value = 0.1518
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group no and group yes is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -399.63379   62.14559
## sample estimates:
##  mean in group no mean in group yes 
##          1403.212          1571.956
t.test(duration ~ y, data = bank)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  duration by y
## t = -18.736, df = 559.97, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group no and group yes is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -360.6134 -292.1772
## sample estimates:
##  mean in group no mean in group yes 
##          226.3475          552.7428
